So, for those of you who do not know, Ouja boards work by a well known group-think style mechanism.

People always expect an outcome from things. Put them all holding a thing on a board, and then ask them a question, and there is going to be one obvious answer. If not, the first few selected letters will make there be one.

The "movement" comes through small twitches in your hands, and small unconscious movements. You are encouraged to "move along with the flow" so if you feel a small movement, you will exaggerate that and push it the way you think it should go.

For example. There have been experiments where you get people at an ouja board, and blindfold them. Then turn the board upside-down. The people at the board will move the little icon thing to the same positions they think the yes/no/letters are, but those icons are not actually there.

Ouja boards are solidly bullshit, and I hope you get that reference.
